We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring which has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH (actually the amide attached to an aniline? Wait: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: that's an amide where the nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH substituent (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH (maybe an aniline). So the amide is N-aryl (anilide) with an ortho? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (para? not specified). So the product is a sulfonamide of p-tolyl sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis using given hints: step1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. In retrosynthesis, we break amide to carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (trans). So forward forms double bond and decarboxylates. In retrosynthesis, we break the double bond to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to amine and sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we can propose route:

Target (T) = sulfonamide (p-tolyl sulfonyl) attached to phenyl ring with α,β-unsaturated amide (trans) attached to aniline.

Step A (retro): disconnect amide bond between carbonyl carbon and aniline nitrogen. Precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (trans) attached to phenyl (the same phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we get intermediate I1: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (attached to phenyl ring) plus aniline.

Step B (retro): disconnect the C=C double bond of the α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. The α,β-unsaturated acid is formed via Doebner from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with aldehyde at para? Actually the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring where the double bond will be formed. So we need aromatic aldehyde: phenyl-CHO (the same phenyl ring). So I1's phenyl-CH=CH-COOH comes from aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) + malonic acid. So retro step yields aromatic aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The sulfonamide part remains attached to the phenyl ring? Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring (the same phenyl that bears the unsaturated acid). So the phenyl ring has both sulfonamide (para to methyl) and the side chain (CH=CH-COOH). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with sulfonamide already present? Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring via nitrogen linking to sulfonyl group. The sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl ring at position 1 (maybe para to methyl). The side chain attaches at position 4? In SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. Let's break: c1ccc(... )cc1 is a tolyl ring (methyl at position). Inside parentheses: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to tolyl ring, and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring (c2...). That second phenyl ring has the unsaturated amide side chain. So the sulfonamide is linking two phenyl rings: tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl, sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So the sulfonamide formation step is between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So retro: break sulfonamide to tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) where aryl is the second phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus step3: sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> target sulfonamide.

Thus we need to generate aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor: the second phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) attached, and also bearing the side chain (α,β-unsaturated amide). So intermediate I2: aryl-SO2Cl with side chain CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH? Wait the side chain includes amide formed later. In retrosynthesis we already broke amide, so side chain is α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl (the same phenyl). So I2 is aryl-SO2Cl with side chain α,β-unsaturated acid (CH=CH-COOH). So after step2 we will have aryl-SO2Cl with aldehyde? Actually step2 is before amide formation, but after sulfonamide formation? The order in forward synthesis: first sulfonyl chloride formation (maybe from aryl sulfonic acid), then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine, then Doebner to make unsaturated acid? Actually the hints order: they enumerated reactions in order they must be applied (forward). They gave three hints: amide formation, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation. That suggests forward order: first sulfonamide formation, then Doebner, then amide coupling? Wait they said "the reactions are enumerated in the order that they must be applied". The hints list: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (amide formation). 2) Doebner modification. 3) sulfonamide formation. So forward: first amide formation (makes amide from acid + amine), then Doebner (makes unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid), then sulfonamide formation (makes sulfonamide). But that seems inconsistent because amide formation requires the unsaturated acid already present, which is product of Doebner. So forward order should be: Doebner (makes unsaturated acid), then amide formation (couple with aniline), then sulfonamide formation (attach sulfonyl chloride to tolyl). However they said enumerated order must be applied, maybe they intend retrosynthetic steps reversed? Actually they said "the reactions are enumerated in the order that they must be applied". So forward synthesis: first amide formation, then Doebner, then sulfonamide formation. That would mean starting from carboxylic acid (maybe unsaturated acid) and amine (aniline) to make amide, then Doebner to make unsaturated acid? That doesn't make sense because Doebner forms unsaturated acid, not amide. So maybe they intend the retrosynthetic direction: we apply retrosynthetic steps in that order (i.e., first break amide, then break double bond, then break sulfonamide). That matches our earlier plan. So we can follow that order.

Thus we need to find templates for each step. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to get template IDs for each transformation.

First step: amide formation reverse (break amide). Need template where functional groups broken: amide (C-N) formed? Actually forward amide formation breaks aliphatic carboxylic acid and forms amide. In retrosynthesis we break amide to carboxylic acid and amine. So we need template where functional_groups_broken includes "amide" and functional_groups_formed includes "aliphatic carboxylic acid" and "primary amines"? But the tool expects forward reaction criteria. So to find template for forward amide formation, we set broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed: amide. That we attempted earlier but got no results. Maybe need to specify "primary amines" broken as well? The forward reaction: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide, breaking O-H and N-H bonds. So broken functional groups: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. Formed: amide. Let's search again with those.
